scope: Kilclone: a very uncertain Patrick-to-Patrick connection
publication_summary: One very uncertain father is newly selected, with no mother. This is a speculative working family connection, not a proved Scotland–Meath migration or an identity merge. The age 60 memorial reading, pre 1707 child problem, uncertain adult identity of the Scottish Patrick and all prior source limitations remain explicit. No original inspection, vital-field change, live WikiTree edit or confidence upgrade is claimed. Working connectivity counts retained profile accounts and inherits the uncertainty in older ancestry. The Gordon 1667 Patrick account is selected as a very uncertain father of the Kilclone Patrick, whose memorial implies birth about 1694. The proposed son predates the Scottish account’s 1707 marriage; no mother or migration is asserted. The two Patricks are retained separately because the memorial age does not fit one-person identity. Largest working family through 1850 grows from 1,018 to 1,022 profiles; separate components 428 to 427; multi-child roots 50 to 49. Three complete comparisons preserve existing records and the memorial family. The study corrects its former deed label to memorial inscription.
